title: Remarks in Accepting Souvenir Presented by the Workmen of the Navy Yard, Bremerton, Wash
occasion: Remarks in Accepting Souvenir Presented by the Workmen of the Navy Yard
paragraphs: I want to thank you and through you your fellow workmen for this token. I also wish to repeat what I have said before, that the victories of Manila and Santiago reflect credit not merely upon those who fought, but upon every man who did his work in preparing the ships for battle. There is not a workman in any of our yards who did his duty in connection with the guns, the armor plate, the turrets, the hulls, or anything, who has not his full right to a share in the credit of those victories. You all did your part in winning them just as much as the men who actually fought. Nothing could have pleased me more than to have received this gift from the men of the yard, and I appreciate it.
